title: Guesstimate: ESG Software Buyers in India

steps.title: 1. Scope & Objective Definition
steps.description: Establish clear boundaries: We are estimating the number of organizations in India with formal ESG reporting mandates or voluntary enterprise sustainability commitments actively procuring dedicated SaaS tools in 2026.
steps.callout: Geography: India | Timeframe: FY26 | Target: B2B Enterprise & Mid-Market

steps.title: 2. Regulatory Mandate Segmentation
steps.description:
Segment the universe into regulatory-driven procurement tiers:
• Tier 1: SEBI BRSR Mandated Top 1,000 Listed Companies (by market cap)
• Tier 2: RBI-Regulated Commercial Banks & Large NBFCs (~135 institutions)
• Tier 3: Global Supply-Chain Exporters under EU CBAM / CSRD pressure (~500 entities)

steps.title: 3. Penetration & Readiness Multipliers
steps.description:
Apply enterprise SaaS readiness and current in-house software penetration:
• Listed top 1,000: 70% currently rely on spreadsheets or generic ERPs and need purpose-built ESG software = 700 buyers
• Financial institutions (135): 60% active procurement for portfolio emissions = 81 buyers
• Global exporters (500): 30% urgency due to EU partner audits = 150 buyers

steps.title: 4. Contract Value & Revenue Math
steps.description:
Compute market size based on tiered Annual Contract Value (ACV):
• Large Enterprise (Top 200 listed): $40,000 ACV × 200 = $8.0M
• Mid-Market Enterprise (581 entities): $20,000 ACV × 581 = $11.6M
• Export SME / Specialized (150 entities): $10,000 ACV × 150 = $1.5M
steps.callout: Total Addressable Domestic ESG SaaS Market = $21.1 Million (~₹175 Crore ARR)

steps.title: 5. Sanity Check & Sensitivity Levers
steps.description: Cross-check against industry analyst reports stating India's green software TAM is expanding at 28% CAGR. Our bottom-up estimate of 931 buyers at ~$21M ARR lands squarely within reasonable economic parameters.
steps.callout: Sanity Check Passed: Matches ~0.8% of India's overall enterprise SaaS spend.

title: Guesstimate: Daily Last-Mile Carbon in Mumbai

steps.title: 1. Scope & System Boundary
steps.description: Calculate daily tailpipe greenhouse gas emissions (Scope 1 & 2) generated by app-based meal delivery fleets operating in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.
steps.callout: Metric: Metric Tonnes CO₂e per Day | Fleet: 2-Wheelers

steps.title: 2. Order Volume & Urban Trip Distance
steps.description:
Mumbai population: ~21M. Middle-to-high income households: ~4M. With an avg order frequency of 0.3 orders/household/day, Mumbai processes ~1.2 Million orders/day across major food delivery platforms.
Average round-trip distance (restaurant pickup + consumer drop + repositioning): 4.8 km.
steps.callout: Daily Fleet Distance Travelled = 1.2M × 4.8 km = 5.76 Million km/day

steps.title: 3. Fleet Powertrain Split
steps.description:
Break down fleet composition:
• Petrol ICE Scooters & Bikes: 85% (~4.90M km/day)
• Commercial Electric 2-Wheelers: 12% (~0.69M km/day)
• Bicycles / Walking couriers: 3% (~0.17M km/day)

steps.title: 4. Emissions Factors & Math
steps.description:
Apply standard GHG Protocol emissions factors:
• Petrol 2-wheelers: ~58 g CO₂e/km → 4.90M km × 58g = 284.2 tCO₂e
• EV (Grid charging intensity @ 0.72 kg/kWh, 0.025 kWh/km): ~18 g CO₂e/km → 0.69M km × 18g = 12.4 tCO₂e
• Bicycles: 0 tCO₂e
steps.callout: Total Baseline = 296.6 Tonnes CO₂e per day (~108,000 tCO₂e annually)

steps.title: 5. Product & Policy Interventions
steps.description: Key PM insight: Shifting 25% of delivery routes to dedicated batching algorithms reduces deadhead kilometers by 18%, saving 53 tonnes of CO₂ daily while lowering delivery partner fuel cost by ₹120/shift.
steps.callout: Product Moat: Algorithmic batching + EV transition = 42% carbon reduction.
